doc: FLOAT64 input points: fbm casts them to float32 first (flat = points.astype(float32)), so the result equals the float32 case on the rounded points. The input stays float64 in the case (the dtype the Python saw); rounding it to float32 first is NOT separable from the chain's own float32 error at this tolerance, so a port that keeps float64 also passes. Chained float32: recomputed in float64, with the matmul written out in both orders, with an alternative lerp and with the points nudged by one float32 ulp either way: the largest observed difference is 5.4e-05; tolerance rtol 1e-4 + atol 0.00054 (10x). The Python casts the points to float32 and accumulates the octaves in float32; neither is enforced (the tolerance was measured with float64 recomputes, so a float64 pipeline passes). The Python evaluates in chunks of 1 << 20 points: a port may chunk differently (checked at build time with chunks of 7 and 97 points: the same field within this tolerance). The permutation input plan<i>.perm is the draw as recorded (256 entries for Perlin3, 1024 for Worley3); the kernel indexes it DOUBLED, concat(perm, perm) (512 or 2048 entries, so p[i + 256] = p[i]): a port that indexes the stored array directly runs off its end (see the .table cases).
